description: We are OrbitLens, a team passionate about space technology, Earth observation, and innovation. Our mission is to explore NASA-ISRO NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data to detect and understand changes on Earth's surface. By turning complex satellite data into clear visualisations and meaningful insights, we aim to support environmental monitoring, disaster awareness, and a better understanding of our changing planet. We believe that every signal reveals a story.
summary:
Orbit Lens is a web app that shows how Malaysia's landscape changes over time using NISAR radar data. Users can search for a location or explore case studies to see ground movement and radar changes every 12 days, with an option to play them as a time-lapse.

The app turns raw data into clear insights, showing changes in land cover (water, vegetation, open land and built-up areas) and ground movement in millimetres. It also suggests possible causes, such as monsoon flooding, paddy seasons, land clearing and land subsidence. Users can compare NISAR's L-band images with C-band data from Sentinel-1 and Canada's RCM.
details:
What It Does

Orbit Lens allows users to explore how Malaysia's landscape changes over time using NISAR satellite radar data. Users can search for a location or explore case studies to view:

  • Ground movement and land changes: Track changes in land cover and ground movement across NISAR's 12-day observation cycles.
  • Time-lapse views: Watch how an area changes over time.
  • Radar polarizations: Compare HH and HV signals to better understand changes in the landscape.
  • Possible causes: Get explanations of what might be driving changes, such as monsoon flooding, paddy farming, land clearing and ground subsidence.
  • Satellite comparison: Compare NISAR's L-band data with Sentinel-1 and Canada's RCM C-band imagery.
  • Environmental context: View flood records, fire hotspots, weather warnings, population data and nearby relief centres.

Users can also compare different dates, download reports, save locations to monitor, receive alerts and submit community reports.

Key Findings (June–October 2026)

We explored several locations to demonstrate how Orbit Lens can help identify environmental changes:

  • Kedah: Detected changes in water, vegetation and agricultural land during the rice-growing season. We also identified limitations in land classification, where flooded rice fields could be mistaken for built-up areas.
  • Kelantan: Established a dry-season baseline before the monsoon, with very little new water detected.
  • Klang Valley: Observed ground movement ranging from -28 mm to +23 mm, but the uncertainty was too high to confidently confirm subsidence.
  • Masamba, Indonesia: Compared the 2020 flash flood using Canada's RCM imagery with more recent NISAR observations.

How It Works

Orbit Lens combines satellite data processing with an interactive web map.

  • Frontend: Built with Next.js, React and MapLibre GL.
  • Satellite processing: Python, NumPy, h5py and pyproj process NISAR radar data.
  • Data sources: NISAR, NASA GIBS, Sentinel-1, RCM, NASA FIRMS, USGS, GDACS, NASA EONET and WorldPop.
  • Backend and hosting: Supabase stores user reports and saved locations, while Vercel and Render host the application and processing service.

The system processes only the satellite data needed for each location instead of downloading entire datasets.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Orbit Lens aims to make satellite radar data accessible to people without specialised remote-sensing knowledge.

It can help disaster management agencies, farmers, planners and local communities monitor flooding, agricultural activity, forest loss and ground movement, even during cloudy weather.

Because it uses publicly available satellite data and works on mobile devices, it offers a more accessible way to understand environmental changes.

What Makes It Different?

  • Turns radar brightness changes into understandable explanations of possible environmental causes.
  • Combines multiple radar polarizations and satellite frequencies.
  • Compares satellite observations across different dates.
  • Shows measurement uncertainty instead of presenting every result as fact.
  • Provides location-based monitoring, reports and alerts in one platform.

Limitations and Considerations

  • NISAR's public data coverage over Malaysia only begins in June 2026, so available observations depend on the archive.
  • Suggested causes are hypotheses, not confirmed explanations.
  • Alerts are marked as unconfirmed and are not automatically sent to authorities.
  • Ground movement measurements include uncertainty, which is displayed to users.
  • Data sources and licensing credits are provided within the app.

Open Source and Links

Orbit Lens is open source under the MIT licence.

  • Live app: https://orbit-lens-v1.vercel.app/
  • GitHub: https://github.com/badrulhanif/orbit-lens-v1

Use of AI

An AI coding assistant (Claude Code) was used to help develop parts of the code and project text. All AI-assisted work was reviewed and tested by the author. Satellite data and findings come from the listed sources; no satellite observations are AI-generated.
